state_map_result.statement: The prepared-state map has real differential rank 12 on an open dense, full-measure subset of the physical angle box. The state locally identifies all 12 angles there. Globally, a generic prepared state in the parameterized image has at least eight angle representatives arising from the first layer alone. These representatives can give different pC even when both encoders are regular.
proof_or_gap: Write C for the ordered CNOT circuit. On computational labels x=(a,b,c) over F₂ it acts by Mx=(b+c,a+b,a+b+c). Remove the final C from the state map, which preserves its rank. Take first-layer y=(π/2,π/2,π/2), all first-layer z=0, and all second-layer angles zero. The first layer prepares |+++⟩ and C fixes it.

Use the X basis |h⟩ₓ=Zʰ|+++⟩ indexed by three-bit labels. At |+⟩, the y and z derivatives give nonzero real and imaginary multiples of |−⟩ respectively. Thus the six second-layer derivatives span the three complex directions labeled 100, 010, 001 over the reals. Pull the whole tangent calculation back through the first C. The six first-layer derivatives now occupy those same three singleton labels, while the second-layer directions move to the labels Mᵀeᵢ because C†ZᵢC=Z^(Mᵀeᵢ). These are 011, 110, 111. All six labels are distinct and orthogonal to the base state. Each supports both real tangent directions, certifying projective rank 12 exactly.

For the density map ρ=|ψ⟩⟨ψ|, the determinant of the 12-by-12 real Hilbert–Schmidt Gram matrix of its derivatives is real analytic and positive at this point. Its zero set has empty interior and measure zero in the connected angle box. The constant-rank theorem gives a local embedding at each regular point. The raw-to-physical tanh map has invertible derivative at every finite raw input.

There is also an exact discrete ambiguity. On any first-layer wire with z≠0 replace (y,z) by (−y,z′), where z′ is z+π reduced into (−π,π). The identity RZ(z′)RY(−y) ∝ RZ(z)RY(y)Z follows by anticommuting Z through the y rotation. Independent choices on the three wires therefore give Uₛ ∝ UZˢ for s∈F₂³, all with the same prepared density. On the open charts where these changes are legal they are local diffeomorphisms, so paired representatives have equal rank.

For an explicit score distinction, take all rotations in V to be identity and take only the first-layer rotations on wire 0 in U to be nontrivial, with y=π/2 and z=π/3. The entanglers cancel in W, leaving RZ(z)RY(π/2) on that wire. The two nonzero return amplitudes W₀ⱼWⱼ₀ are e^(−iz)/2 and −1/2. The wire-0 branch flip reverses their relative sign, giving pC=1/4 and 3/4. More generally, pC(W)−pC(WZ₀) is analytic in both encoders' angles and this example makes it nonzero. Hence the distinction holds on an open dense, full-measure set of angle pairs, including pairs where both encoders are regular and all eight chart representatives are legal.
state_map_result.generic_vs_singular: Any smoothly varying same-state angle curve with nonzero velocity lies in the rank-deficient set wherever it moves. This accounts for the supplied continuous z witness. The first-layer branch flips give a different answer for separated points of a fiber. Generic local identifiability coexists with generic discrete, score-visible completion ambiguity. Eight is a lower bound on generic fiber multiplicity in the angle domain.
state_map_result.implications: On a single regular inverse chart, pC factors locally through the pair of prepared states because each state recovers its encoder angles. Across charts, the same pair of densities can entail different scores. A text encoder may occupy only one chart or correlate its chart choices with features already recoverable from the states. The mathematical ambiguity alone therefore establishes no missing task information on text.

selected_direction.claim: The eight completion choices give an exact finite experiment for the normalized readout. A shared choice across tokens preserves every prepared density, p1, pS and pD. Its task-visible effect admits a seven-coefficient formula that includes cancellation across tokens, attention normalization and the values.
selected_direction.theorem: Fix one logit row, its tokens, real values uₜ, bias b and ε=10⁻⁶. Apply the same first-layer branch s to every U in the row while holding every V fixed. Assume the affected z angles are nonzero for a literal interior-angle realization. Put aₜⱼ=(Wₜ)₀ⱼ(Wₜ)ⱼ₀ and gₜₖ=Σⱼ aₜⱼ conjugate(aₜ,ⱼ⊕ₖ), with indices in F₂³ and ⊕ denoting bitwise addition. Let Nₛ=Σₜ(pC(WₜZˢ)+ε), Lₛ the resulting logit, and N_D,L_D the analogous dephased quantities at the same parameters. Define Hₖ=Σₜ(uₜ+b−L_D)gₜₖ for k≠0. Then Nₛ(Lₛ−L_D)=Σₖ≠₀ (−1)^(s·k)Hₖ. Consequently L_D=Σₛ NₛLₛ/(8N_D), and (1/8)Σₛ [Nₛ(Lₛ−L_D)]²=Σₖ≠₀ Hₖ². The row logit is invariant across all eight branches exactly when all seven Hₖ vanish. The trained branch s=0 has displacement Σₖ≠₀ Hₖ/N₀, which can vanish even with positive branch variance.
selected_direction.proof: Right multiplication by Zˢ multiplies aₜⱼ by the character (−1)^(s·j). It preserves both |W₀₀| and every |aₜⱼ|. Expanding the squared modulus of the signed return sum and grouping by j⊕j′=k gives pC(WₜZˢ)=Σₖ(−1)^(s·k)gₜₖ. Each coefficient is real by exchanging the two indices, and gₜ₀=pD(Wₜ). Multiplying the normalized logit difference by Nₛ gives Σₜ(uₜ+b−L_D)(pC(WₜZˢ)+ε). Its constant coefficient vanishes by the definition of L_D, leaving the claimed seven coefficients. Character orthogonality gives the mean and mean-square formulas, using ΣₛNₛ=8N_D. Positivity of the denominators gives the invariance criterion.
selected_direction.standard_parts: The rotation identity, Walsh autocorrelation expansion, character orthogonality and Parseval identity are standard. The application-specific result is that this encoder realizes the entire character group on its own completion fibers, and that its matched dephased logit is exactly the denominator-weighted center of the resulting normalized logits. The Hₖ identify precisely which path correlations survive the fixed value readout.
selected_direction.genuinely_unresolved_part: Whether the independently trained coherent model uses its realized branch to improve TRAIN predictions is empirical. The branch transformation is shared at the circuit-input level. Representability of every transformed angle function by the original classical text-to-raw network would require a separate argument. At z=0 a flipped wire requires an endpoint for this angle formula. The matrix identity and logit theorem still apply to the limiting completion WZˢ.
selected_direction.boundary: Take a two-token row with identical W on both tokens, using the one-wire example above, and distinct values u₁,u₂. A branch flip changes both raw scores from 1/4 to 3/4. Both attention weights remain 1/2 and every Hₖ vanishes. Thus even an order-one score difference on a true completion fiber can disappear exactly at the task readout.

diagnostic.observable: At the final coherent checkpoint, compute the ordinary supervised TRAIN loss eight times on the same fixed examples, using WₜZˢ in the coherent score with one common s across all tokens, rows and examples. Keep features, values, biases and ε fixed. Use the single paired contrast Δ=(1/7)Σₛ≠₀ loss(s)−loss(0). This tests whether the realized completion improves predictions relative to a uniformly chosen nonidentity shared flip.
diagnostic.fixed_samples_rule: After the fixed full study, use the first 64 distinct TRAIN examples in the existing deterministic data order, or all if fewer. Use evaluation mode and keep every token normally used for those examples. Compute from the return amplitudes directly. Any exact zero in an affected first-layer z uses the limiting-completion interpretation above.
diagnostic.comparison: Compare the trained orientation to the seven flips at that same coherent checkpoint. This holds every individual path magnitude fixed and tests the signs after normalization and value aggregation. The independently optimized dephased arm answers a different training question.
diagnostic.falsification: Δ≤0 falsifies the specified interpretation that the realized orientation improves mean loss against these shared completion flips on this TRAIN slice. A positive Δ supports orientation sensitivity in the fitted predictor. It cannot establish that text requires process access or that this sensitivity accounts for a held-out gain.

result.claim_ceiling: The exact claims concern generic local angle recovery, global completion ambiguity, and normalized logit variation within a specified eight-element orbit of the fixed circuit. The supplied singular witness and raw-Gram obstruction retain their stated scopes. Task necessity, superiority under independent training, novelty priority, classical hardness and quantum speedup remain unestablished.
